movement_source: row 'Net profit excluding Notable Items', column FY24 (Sept 24) -> column FY25 (Sept 25)
headline: Westpac's cash earnings (net profit excluding Notable Items) fell $141 million (-2%) to $6,972 million in FY25 from $7,113 million in FY24. Total operating income grew 3% to $22,464 million, while pre-provision profit declined 3% to $10,548 million due to a $972 million increase in operating expenses. This was partially offset by a $113 million reduction in credit impairment charges and stable tax expense.

drivers.narrative: NII increased $557 million (+3%) to $19,473 million. Growth was driven by volume expansion: average loans rose 4% ($31.7 billion), particularly business loans (+11%), which supported revenue despite margin pressure from competitive deposit pricing.

Other operating income rose $144 million (+5%) to $2,991 million. Net fees grew $60 million (+4%) to $1,732 million, and wealth management income increased $35 million (+8%) to $476 million, reflecting higher client activity.

Underlying operating expenses increased $699 million (+6%) to $11,643 million (excluding the $273 million restructuring charge). Staff costs rose $427 million (+7%) to $6,326 million, and technology expenses grew $372 million (+13%) to $3,136 million.

A $273 million 'Fit for Growth' restructuring charge was incurred in H2 FY25. This is reported as a notable item and excluded from the cash earnings metric, but it represents a real cash outflow that reduced statutory profit.

Credit impairment charges decreased $113 million (-21%) to $424 million. The lower provision rate reflected stable credit quality and favorable movements in expected loss models, contributing positively to the year-on-year earnings comparison.

Tax expense decreased slightly by $34 million (-1%) to $3,135 million. The effective tax rate remained stable at 30.97%, up just 13 basis points from 30.84%, resulting in a small positive contribution to net profit growth.

notable_items: Restructuring charge of $273 million in H2 FY25.
limitations: The bridge reconciles the change in 'Net profit excluding Notable Items'. Statutory profit moved differently (-$74 million) due to the inclusion of the $273 million restructuring charge and other notable items.
Expenses are claimed on the underlying/notable split; the bank equally publishes the combined headline framing, so both claims are capped at 80.
